LESSON: AUDIENCE AWARENESS

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.4: Audience Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Audience Awareness. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when speaker and the listener is varied. The further away?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Demonstrate awareness of own voice in and out of class.
2. Speak clearly when talking to others in and out of class.
3. Speak loudly enough for the audience to hear in school and at home
4. Experience pleasure in varying own voice when communicating with others. own voice accordingly to meet the needs of the listener. recorded audio clips. The volume could be deliberately raised or lowered and the learners encouraged to say how this affects their hearing. be involved in presenting songs, poems and rhymes in class and during parade.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Demonstrate awareness of own voice in and out of class.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate awareness of own voice in and out of class. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Speak clearly when talking to others in and out of class.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to speak clearly when talking to others in and out of class. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Speak loudly enough for the audience to hear in school and at home
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to speak loudly enough for the audience to hear in school and at home. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. Experience pleasure in varying own voice when communicating with others. own voice accordingly to meet the needs of the listener. recorded audio clips. The volume could be deliberately raised or lowered and the learners encouraged to say how this affects their hearing. be involved in presenting songs, poems and rhymes in class and during parade.

The volume could be deliberately raised or lowered and the learners encouraged to say how this affects their hearing. be involved in presenting songs, poems and rhymes in class and during parade. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Audience Awareness.
2. Explain Audience Awareness to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Audience Awareness.
4. Show that you can: Demonstrate awareness of own voice in and out of class.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Audience Awareness. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: when speaker and the listener is varied. The further away?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Demonstrate awareness of own voice in and out of class.
2. Speak clearly when talking to others in and out of class.
3. Speak loudly enough for the audience to hear in school and at home
4. Experience pleasure in varying own voice when communicating with others. own voice accordingly to meet the needs of the listener. recorded audio clips. The volume could be deliberately raised or lowered and the learners encouraged to say how this affects their hearing. be involved in presenting songs, poems and rhymes in class and during parade.
